Summary
Jack writes to Folks and Ruth about the end of World War II, specifically Victory in Europe (V-E) Day, and his personal excitement about the demobilization plans. He mentions the point system for demobilization and the need for reinforcements. He also expresses concern about the health of his family and extends greetings and thanks for Mother's Day.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_31a) --- Dear Folks and Ruth, I know it has been a long time since I've written last. I guess I was a bit too emotionally moved over world-shaking events during the past few weeks to have the patience to write. At any rate, I think you're used to these periodic silences from me. First came news of Helen's death and then that long-awaited V-E day. It's not easy here to go into feelings about Victory in Europe. I've saved all the daily papers and will send them to you soon. On a picture of V-day in Australia, celebrations were practically non-existent a very sober. No one got too excited outwardly but there was joy in every heart. With the Jap war front going full blast people over here did not seem too concerned with the end of the war in Europe. Except of course it meaning that all the United States units can concentrate on drowning the Japs. We are expecting plenty of reinforcements. You'll get a better picture of things when you receive these newspapers I'll send. For myself, you can well imagine the intense personal excitement at not seeing them in [illegible] and one [illegible] to VE the [illegible] as a [illegible] forces [illegible] with the [illegible] day Army announced its demobilization plans; you probably read about the point system --- Page 2 (Beckerman_31b) --- 2. surpapern with a numm of 85 pts a la demobligation. However, there so hany ifs and buts to the picture, that it won't affect us very much over here. - not until the Japs are beaten anyway. I have a total of 62 points - which the out sally would mean that if I stood overseas for another year I evaned the eligible for demobligator. But we're counting on finishing the job before then. Is there much talk of the point system at home? Received your V-mail yesterday which was post marked the 25th April. That's pretty bad time so you had better go back to air mail. By the way I can't answer your V-mail questions even in an indirect manner, in my personal letters. I can only tell you where I've gone after I get there. I was quite disturbed about your last letter where Ruth told about everyone having health troubles. Please take care of yourselves until we get home. I know that will be a good time. And don't worry - you it shouldn't be too long. I'm sure we are going into winter uniforms as it has gotten quite cold. We've got swamped with so much work that I've got to assist me and a couple --- Page 3 (Beckerman_31c) --- 3 men for my section. It's been keep. You should have received those photographs by now and hope everybody's enjoyed them. I wish you would send me the a copy of the last Bulletin which I haven't received as yet. I understand there's an article in there about my old Murray Sanger. She wrote me about it. I never wrote you about Sanger because somehow or other I was under the impression it was trying to be kept a secret (in order to be with held from his mother). I was, and still am, plenty disturbed about it. Last month was Ruth's birthday and I want to extend my greetings could do better if I was home. And this month covering Mother's Day likewise goes sincere thanks and appreciation to Mama and Papa for all their hardships and sacrifices these past few years. Sincerely, Love and Regards, Jack.
